problem_statement: Develop an offline AI assisted imaging tool that enhances low quality ultrasound videos using denoising and contrast adjustment, then highlights potential cysts or other anomalies using computer vision. The system generates annotated images with confidence scores for remote radiologist review, supporting healthcare workers using affordable ultrasound equipment in resource limited settings.
medical_disclaimer: ScanSure AI is an experimental AI-assisted ultrasound image enhancement and analysis tool. It does not provide a medical diagnosis. All findings require review by a qualified radiologist.
audio_stream_report: No audio stream present in input video.

dataset_provenance.reference_distribution: BUSI (Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset, Al-Dhabyani et al., 2020) + Physics-Grounded B-Mode Acoustic Phantom Sequences
dataset_provenance.temporal_validation_limitation: Public breast ultrasound datasets (such as BUSI, 780 still images across normal, benign, and malignant cases) contain static 2D keyframes rather than continuous cine loops. While temporal consistency is validated on synthetic acoustic cine phantoms, clinical video-level temporal validation requires prospective multi-center cine loop trials.

calibration.score_type: Unnormalized Multi-Scale Segmentation Logit Sigmoid Score (Raw Model Confidence)
calibration.calibration_note: Raw neural/feature segmentation scores are reported alongside the empirically validated threshold (0.55). Detections scoring between 0.55 and 0.72 or exhibiting heterogeneous internal echoes are explicitly flagged as 'Uncertain — Requires Radiologist Review'.

detection_summary.target_workflow: Remote Radiologist Review for Rural Healthcare Workers (Low-Cost Portable Ultrasound)
detection_summary.confidence_disclosure: Reported scores are raw uncalibrated segmentation model scores, NOT calibrated clinical probabilities. Findings scoring between the validated threshold and 0.72 are flagged as 'Uncertain — Requires Radiologist Review'.

enhancement_evaluation.clinical_interpretation_note: PSNR and SSIM measure structural fidelity relative to the raw B-mode acquisition, while ENL (Equivalent Number of Looks) and EPI (Edge Preservation Index) quantify speckle reduction and anatomical boundary retention. Higher quantitative metrics alone do not establish diagnostic efficacy and require radiologist review.
